first_sentence: I'm not okay with 1 % risk, then that's me.
transcript: I'm not okay with 1 % risk, then that's me. There's not many people that pretty much I know personally that pretty much only risk 1 % of living like how I live. They talk a lot about dynamic risk, meaning that when they have edge and they can see it and they have that gut feeling of that edge is in this trade, they then look to size it, and they'll size it a lot more heavier into those particular trades rather than just sticking static 1 % consistently. What were your thoughts on that? Have you seen a pattern in that as well? A number of traders pointed out that when you have real strong confidence on a trade, you have to step on the accelerator. Like I think of particularly like Stanley Druckenmiller and he gives a story where he got very bullish on the DMAR. He goes into Soros' office and he gives him his whole pitch and Soros asks him, you know, how big is your position? He says, a billion. He says, you call that a position? The point being, if you're that sure, this is why you only have a billion on it. He credits Soros with teaching him that it's important to be a pig when the opportunity is there. When he had the opportunity, it was really a big opportunity to even, as he said, step on the accelerator.
